Association to Function Knowledge Portal update

The Association to Function Knowledge Portal (A2FKP) continues to grow. It currently includes 595 genetic association datasets covering 668 traits and diseases; credible sets for 78 phenotypes; over 5,500 epigenomic annotation datasets; and 65 lists of predicted effector genes for 52 phenotypes. We analyze and distill these data, using multiple bioinformatic methods, to present both summaries that are meaningful to the non-geneticist researcher and sophisticated tools that allow geneticists to do custom expert analyses.

The Knowledge Portal Network includes a suite of Community Portals that are developed in collaboration with disease-focused researchers. Each displays a subset of the data in A2FKP that is tailored to the interests and needs of that research community, as well as other community-specific content and data types. Our flagship portal, the Type 2 Diabetes Knowledge Portal (T2DKP), is a community portal within A2FKP, as are other portals for 12 other disease areas. This Fall, we’ll add two new community portals: the Aging Knowledge Portal (AKP) and the Kidney Disease Knowledge Portal (KDKP).

New gene expression viewer on Gene pages

The new gene expression viewer on the Gene pages of all portals displays tissue-specific expression levels in a plot and table. The default view shows aggregate results in a tissue category such as “adipose tissue”, and you can drill down to view results from individual datasets in specific tissue or cell types (for example, “subcutaneous adipose tissue”).You can filter the data by multiple criteria, and navigate to the dataset records at the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas (CMDGA). The viewer currently displays bulk RNA-seq data, and we’ll be adding single-cell expression data in the future.

The Gene Finder tool is now the Gene Sifter

We’ve added many new filtering criteria to the Gene Finder tool–so many that we’ve renamed it the Gene Sifter. This tool allows you to assemble a custom set of genes based on their gene-level genetic association scores from common variants and then add and filter by rare variant associations, Human Genetic Evidence Calculator scores, tissue-specific gene expression levels, and presence on a list of predicted effector genes for one or more traits. Find it under the “KP Labs” menu on all the Knowledge Portals.

Human Genetic Evidence Calculator implemented at scale

The first iteration of our Human Genetic Evidence (HuGE) Calculator was available as an interactive tool that enabled you to find the HuGE score, representing the weight of genetic evidence for involvement of a gene in a disease or trait of interest, for one gene/trait combination at a time. That tool is still available (under the "KP Labs" menu of all Knowledge Portals), with several options to customize the output, but now we’ve also implemented the method at scale in our back-end Aggregator, so that precomputed HuGE scores are available for each gene across all phenotypes represented in the Knowledge Portals. The scores are represented in a PheWAS plot on the Gene page, and are also available via the Gene Sifter.

Predicted Effector Genes Knowledge Portal

We continue to curate lists of predicted effector genes from the literature (65 lists to date), and we’ve collected these on a Predicted Effector Genes Knowledge Portal (PEGKP) that allows you to search the lists by gene, trait, or publication. The lists are now much more accessible: Gene and Phenotype pages now display links to the relevant lists, and presence of a gene on an effector list can also be added to Gene Sifter results. Find PEGKP at the "Predicted Effector Genes" link under the "KP Labs" menu of all Knowledge Portals, and please contact us if you have generated a list that you would like to share on the Knowledge Portals!

Upload your own data!

We have been working on a Data Registry that allows researchers to upload their own datasets to the Knowledge Portals. It’s still a beta version, but we would welcome feedback on the interface as we develop it further. If you have a dataset to contribute and you would like to help us by testing the interface, please let us know!

Programmatic access

Did you know that we offer programmatic access to Knowledge Portal data via our BioIndex? You can query and download genetic associations, epigenomic annotations, bioinformatic method results, and much more. We’re still working to improve and document the interface. If you’ve used it, we’d really appreciate your feedback!

AMP® CMD news

As part of our role in the Accelerating Medicines Partnership® in Common Metabolic Disease, we administer an Opportunity Pool (OP) to fund projects that address gaps in the currently funded research. Proposals for Cycle 3 of the OP are now under review by AMP CMD steering committee members. There will be two more cycles of OP funding in the future, so get your proposals ready!

New direction for the KP team: a tissue-specific portal

Most of the portals in the Knowledge Portal Network focus on a disease area, with the exception of the Lipid Droplet Knowledge Portal, centering on an organelle and its biological role. Building on this work, we’re now beginning to develop a resource devoted to a human tissue. A grant awarded to co-P.I.s Evan Rosen, Melina Claussnitzer, Orr Ashenberg, Noël Burtt, and Jason Flannick will support the Human Adipose Tissue Knowledge Portal, which will provide access to results from single-cell RNA sequencing in different adipose tissue depots and other functional assays to increase our knowledge about this tissue that is critically important to human health.

Knowledge Portal publications

We've recently published two papers on the Knowledge Portals:

Costanzo MC, von Grotthuss M, Massung J, Jang D, Caulkins L, Koesterer R, Gilbert C, et al. The Type 2 Diabetes Knowledge Portal: An open access genetic resource dedicated to type 2 diabetes and related traits. Cell Metab. 2023 Apr 4;35(4):695-710.e6. doi: 10.1016/j.cmet.2023.03.001.

Kudtarkar P, et al. Leveraging type 1 diabetes human genetic and genomic data in the T1D knowledge portal. PLoS Biol. 2023 Aug 10;21(8):e3002233. doi: 10.1371/journal.pbio.3002233.
